q0454: Secure remote access to internal resources without exposing them to the internet = VPN.
q0455: New or renewed certificate: generate a key pair and submit a CSR to the CA.
q0456: Many log types in one place, with correlation and alerting = SIEM.
q0457: Who secures what in the cloud, for each service model = the shared responsibility matrix.
q0458: Script injected into a page that runs in the victim's browser = XSS (stored, reflected or DOM-based).
q0459: One workstation opening sessions to many servers at once = concurrent session usage, a sign of possible lateral movement.
q0460: Stop privileged credentials being stolen and reused (pass-the-hash) = PAM with vaulted, short-lived credentials.
q0461: Identification (claim) → authentication (prove) → authorization (what you may access) → accounting (what you did).
q0462: Personal information about employees or customers = privacy data, governed by privacy policies and laws.
q0463: Insiders use valid access, so catch them with behavioral analytics (UBA/UEBA) that flags unusual activity.
q0464: Track changes to code, including infrastructure as code = version control (such as Git).
q0465: Prioritize vulnerabilities by CVSS, adjusted for how exposed and critical each asset is.
q0466: A formal agreement on how two organizations collaborate and handle shared IP = MOA.
q0468: Physical access control = something that opens the door only for the right person: swipe cards and biometrics. Cameras only record.
q0469: Malware from an external drive → removable media training: never plug in unknown devices.
q0470: Prove a DR site really works (data and capacity) = run a failover to it.
q0471: Worrying about the business consequences of a failure = business impact analysis (BIA).
q0472: VM escape = breaking out of a guest into the hypervisor, exposing the host and every other VM on it.
q0473: Proper sanitization stops data being recovered from used drives.
q0474: Stop unknown devices on a wall or phone port = MAC filtering (or port security and 802.1X).
q0475: The procedures and boundaries a pen tester must follow = rules of engagement.
q0476: Creating forensic images = acquisition. Keeping them unaltered = preservation.
q0477: Timing a network-delivered IoT exploit = firewall logs; IoT devices rarely run endpoint agents.
q0478: A shared backup privileged account that must work even if SSO fails = a PAM vault.
q0479: Defacing a site for attention and bragging rights = unskilled attacker (script kiddie).
q0480: Data stored abroad but still subject to its home country's laws = data sovereignty.
q0481: Proof for outsiders that testing was done = third-party attestation.
q0482: Fine-tune who can read or write a specific file = its ACL.
q0483: Step-by-step instructions to do a task the same way every time (patching to the baseline) = SOP.
